assumptions.condition: The potential-outcome schedule \(Y\) is fixed under the assignment draw.
The treatment-indexed potential-observation schedule \(O\) is fixed under the assignment draw.

standard.name: fixed potential missingness indicators in design-based inference

assumptions.condition: The support \(\Omega\) is a nonempty explicitly listed subset of \(\mathcal Z_m\).

standard.name: known assignment probabilities on a finite support

assumptions.condition: Conditional on \(\mathscr G\), the final assignment obeys the recorded mass function \(w\) on the recorded support \(\Omega\).

definitions.name: Legal sharp-null completion set
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal C_\delta(a)=\{b\in\mathbb R^I:b_i=Y_i(a_i)-\delta a_i\text{ for every }i\text{ with }O_i(a_i)=1\}\).

definitions.name: Midrank oracle tail
definitions.construction: For \(b\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\), set \(r_i(b)=1+\#\{j:b_j<b_i\}+\{\#\{j:b_j=b_i\}-1\}/2\), \(T(z,b)=\sum_i z_i r_i(b)\), and \(p(a,b)=\sum_{z\in\Omega}w_z\mathbf 1\{T(z,b)\ge T(a,b)\}\).

definitions.name: Complete weak-order chamber complex
definitions.construction: \(\mathfrak W_\delta(a)=\{\preceq:\preceq\text{ is a total preorder on }I\text{ and some }b\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\text{ satisfies }i\preceq j\Longleftrightarrow b_i\le b_j\}\); its cells retain both strict gaps and equality blocks.

definitions.name: Reversible weak-order insertion
definitions.construction: Sort the distinct observed values into \(g\) ordered blocks; for each missing label, branch by inserting it into any of the current gaps or attaching it to any current block; at each final ordered partition evaluate all \(L\) weighted tail inequalities and retain a maximizer.

definitions.name: Equality-aware effect inversion
definitions.construction: Compute \(\mathcal B(a)\), evaluate \(\mathsf{ChamberMax}\) once on every open component of \(\mathbb R\setminus\mathcal B(a)\) and once at every point of \(\mathcal B(a)\), and return exactly those cells on which \(P_\delta(a)>\alpha\).

definitions.name: Guard--vertex--edge weighted-support reduction
definitions.construction: For a nontrivial \(\textsc{Clique}\) instance \((G,s)\), use \(v\) missing vertex units, \(h=2v-s\) observed outcome-one anchors, and four observed outcome-zero controls. The realized row treats all vertex and anchor units and has unnormalized weight \(1\). For each vertex \(i\), a guard row exchanges vertex \(i\) for one control and has weight \(A_\star\); a vertex row exchanges vertex \(i\) and one anchor for two controls and has weight \(B\); for each edge \(ij\in E\), an edge row exchanges vertices \(i,j\) and two anchors for four controls and has weight \(1\). Normalize by \(W_\star\) and use threshold \(q_\star\).

definitions.name: Constrained six-unit non-extreme witness
definitions.construction: Let \(n=6\), \(m=3\), baseline balance scores be \((-6,-1,2,2,-8,7)\), and retain assignments whose absolute treated-minus-control score is at most \(4\). Then \(\Omega=\{\{1,2,6\},\{1,3,4\},\{2,5,6\},\{3,4,5\}\}\) with weights \(1/4\); take \(a=\{1,2,6\}\), unit \(1\) missing, and observed baseline outcomes on units \(2,\ldots,6\) equal to \((1,2,3,4,5)\).

definitions.name: Two-vertex equality-face witness
definitions.construction: Apply \(\mathsf R(G,s)\) to the graph consisting of one edge with \(v=s=2\); then \(B=2\), \(A_\star=6\), and \(W_\star=18\).

definitions.name: Encoded explicit-support decision language
definitions.construction: An input is \(\langle a,\delta,\{(i,y_i^{\mathrm{obs},\delta}):i\notin M(a)\},\Omega,\{w_z:z\in\Omega\},q\rangle\), where \(\delta\), the observed coordinates, the weights, and \(q\) are rational, \(\Omega\) is listed row by row, and the total binary length is \(\ell\). The input is accepted exactly when some \(b\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\) has \(p(a,b)\ge q\).

definitions.name: Parameterized-complexity handle
definitions.construction: Use \(\mathsf{ParamFrontier}\) to seek either a dynamic program whose state consists of support-column types and current tie-block sufficient statistics, or a parameter-preserving replacement of rational weights by explicit support gadgets that retains the lowest-tied-block converse.

statements.statement: Every cell of \(\mathfrak W_\delta(a)\) fixes the full midrank vector, every value \(T(z,b)\), and every indicator in \(p(a,b)\). Hence \(P_\delta(a)\) is a maximum over the finite complete weak-order complex, equality faces included, and is attained. If the observed outcomes are rational, every nonempty cell has a rational representative of polynomial encoding length.
statements.justification: This theorem converts an unbounded missing-outcome optimization into a finite exact object without discarding ties.
statements.gap: Li, Sheng, and Yu obtain an extreme-completion closed form from an exchangeable assignment law together with an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention. Ordinary midranks under arbitrary explicitly listed rational assignment weights instead require the equality-inclusive chamber maximum.
statements.consumer: It supplies a checkable finite certificate for exact attrition-robust testing under rerandomization and other restricted designs.

statements.statement: Under \(H_\delta\), for every fixed potential-outcome schedule, every fixed treatment-indexed observation schedule, and every \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), \(\Pr_w\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}\le\alpha\). Consequently \(\Pr_w\{\delta\in\mathcal I_\alpha(A)\}\ge1-\alpha\).
statements.justification: Pointwise domination of the infeasible oracle tail yields unconditional finite-sample size control despite treatment-dependent observation.
statements.gap: General Fisher validity is known from Luo et al.; Li, Sheng, and Yu study worst-case completion under exchangeability and altered index tie-breaking; and Heng, Zhang, and Feng establish imputation-assisted randomization validity through re-imputation. None evaluates the equality-complete supplied-support Wilcoxon-midrank envelope stated here.
statements.consumer: An analyst can report a finite-population exact confidence set without conditioning on the realized survivor set.

statements.statement: The algorithm \(\mathsf{ChamberMax}\) computes \(P_\delta(a)\) and an optimizing weak-order certificate using at most \(\prod_{j=0}^{k-1}\{2(g+j)+1\}\le(2n+1)^k\) leaves and \(O((2n+1)^k nL\,\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\) bit operations. For \(k=1\), an equality-inclusive sweep through the \(2g+1\) positions runs in \(O(nL\,\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\) after sorting. This is an \(\mathrm{XP}\), not an \(\mathrm{FPT}\), guarantee.
statements.justification: The bound locates the exact tractable regime and gives a sharp practical routine when attrition is small.
statements.gap: Sills computes a fixed tied-rank distribution, and Mehta, Patel, and Wei exploit special design recursions; neither enumerates completion weak orders for a supplied weighted support.
statements.consumer: Small-attrition cluster trials can compute the exact robust p-value rather than use Monte Carlo completion searches.

statements.statement: The function \(\delta\mapsto P_\delta(a)\) is constant on every open component of \(\mathbb R\setminus\mathcal B(a)\), while a singleton breakpoint may have a distinct equality-face value. Since \(|\mathcal B(a)|\le n^2\), \(\mathsf{Invert}\) returns the complete, possibly disconnected confidence set \(\mathcal I_\alpha(a)\), including exact endpoint status, with \(O(n^2)\) calls to \(\mathsf{ChamberMax}\).
statements.justification: Finite equality-aware inversion replaces a grid and does not assume a monotone or connected p-value curve.
statements.gap: Luo et al. give careful Fisher inversion and Caughey et al. use effect-increasing ranks, but neither handles optimizer changes caused by an attrition envelope on a weighted support.
statements.consumer: Applied researchers obtain every accepted additive effect and its correct open or closed boundary.

statements.statement: In the six-unit construction, any completion with the missing outcome below \(1\) gives supported rank sums \((9,8,13,12)\) and upper tail \(3/4\), whereas any completion strictly between \(1\) and \(2\) gives \((9,9,12,12)\) and upper tail \(1\). Thus an interior completion strictly dominates the lower extreme even though both completions have no outcome ties.
statements.justification: The witness isolates why exchangeable extreme-imputation logic fails under a covariate-constrained support.
statements.gap: The extreme-completion simplification of Li, Sheng, and Yu uses an exchangeable assignment law and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention. This support is uniform and complement-symmetric but balance-restricted, and ordinary midranks make an interior completion optimal.
statements.consumer: It gives a regression test for any implementation and prevents an invalid endpoint-only optimizer.

statements.statement: For any subset \(S\subseteq I\) of cardinality \(t\) and any completed midrank vector, \(\sum_{i\in S}r_i(b)\ge t(t+1)/2\). Equality holds if and only if every label in \(S\) is strictly below every label outside \(S\). In particular, if \(t\) labels all have rank at most \((t+1)/2\), they form the unique lowest tied block and each has rank \((t+1)/2\).
statements.justification: The equality characterization is the load-bearing converse that prevents tie faces from creating false graph certificates.
statements.gap: Classical midrank identities give the total rank sum, but the subset equality condition is the exact combinatorial lemma required by this reduction.
statements.consumer: A machine-checked version closes the remaining proof bottleneck in the NP-hardness argument.

statements.statement: \(\textsc{Explicit-Max-Tail}\), whose encoded instance consists of \(a\), a rational \(\delta\), every labeled rational coordinate \(y_i^{\mathrm{obs},\delta}\) with \(i\notin M(a)\), the support \(\Omega\) listed row by row, every rational weight \(w_z\), and a rational threshold \(q\), is NP-complete. Membership in NP is certified by a complete weak order together with a rational representative \(b\in\mathcal C_\delta(a)\) of polynomial encoding length; a polynomial-time verifier checks the observed-coordinate equalities, the represented weak order and midranks, and the exact rational weighted tail inequality \(p(a,b)\ge q\). NP-hardness holds for instances \(\mathsf R(G,s)\) with \(v\) missing realized-treated outcomes, four realized controls, two distinct observed outcome values, \(n=3v-s+4\) units, and \(1+2v+|E|\) explicitly listed rows with polynomial-bit rational weights. A completion reaches \(q_\star\) if and only if its \(s\) lowest tied missing labels induce an \(s\)-clique in \(G\).
statements.justification: The result shows that the chamber explosion reflects intrinsic completion difficulty rather than a naive implementation.
statements.gap: The exact-test literature reports combinatorial cost but supplies no decision-complexity classification for a rationally weighted explicit support with missing midranks.
statements.consumer: Software can justify exact fixed-\(k\) computation and principled approximation when attrition is large.

statements.statement: For the two-vertex equality-face construction, tying both missing outcomes strictly below the controls yields \(P_\delta(a)=1\), while maximizing over strict weak-order chambers only yields \(8/9\).
statements.justification: This smallest reduction instance proves that equality faces are inferentially active.
statements.gap: Tie-aware fixed-data tests retain average ranks, but no prior supplied-design completion result proves a strict loss from deleting equality strata.
statements.consumer: It is a mandatory unit test for chamber enumeration and for the reduction converse.

statements.statement: Suppose randomized clusters are the units in \(I\), each has a prespecified finite scalar endpoint \(Y_i(d)\), and \(\mathscr G\) is fixed before the final assignment draw. Under the recorded conditional law, \(\Pr\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\mid\mathscr G\}\le\alpha\), and therefore \(\Pr\{P_\delta(A)\le\alpha\}\le\alpha\). The support and its probabilities remain unchanged across completions; no conditioning on survivors or on the selected row is permitted.
statements.justification: The corollary turns a saved constrained allocation space into a valid prospective attrition-robust rank analysis.
statements.gap: Yu et al.'s \(\texttt{cptest}\) uses residualized cluster-mean contrasts, and Hennessy et al. do not address missing-completion midranks.
statements.consumer: A new \(\texttt{cvcrand}\) rank option can analyze a prespecified cluster endpoint while preserving the design actually used.

statements.statement: Determine whether \(\textsc{Explicit-Max-Tail}\), parameterized by \(k\), admits an \(f(k)\operatorname{poly}(n,L,\ell)\) exact algorithm or is \(\mathrm{W}[1]\)-hard. Separately determine whether either conclusion survives when the input support is uniform and generated by a fixed-dimensional balance rule; no such hardness is asserted here.
statements.justification: The theorem-level XP and NP-completeness results leave the genuine parameterized boundary unresolved.
statements.gap: Neither exact rank computation nor missing-data testing currently classifies this parameter, and the weighted reduction does not answer the uniform balance-generated case.
statements.consumer: The answer determines whether large trials with a modest number of missing endpoints need approximation or can have fixed-parameter exact inference.

sampling_model.design: A known rationally weighted fixed-count randomization law on the explicitly listed support \(\Omega\).
sampling_model.units: A fixed finite population with fixed potential outcomes \(Y_i(0),Y_i(1)\) and fixed treatment-indexed observation indicators \(O_i(0),O_i(1)\).
sampling_model.treatment: The random vector \(A\) is the only stochastic object and has exactly \(m\) treated units.
sampling_model.overlap: Every listed assignment has strictly positive recorded probability; no unit-level marginal-positivity condition is imposed.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: There is no sampled nuisance function. Missing sharp-null baseline coordinates range over \(\mathcal C_\delta(a)\) and are eliminated by the finite weak-order maximum.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Under an exchangeable assignment law and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention, the supremum Fisher p-value over attrition completions has an extreme-completion closed form.

Imputation-assisted randomization tests that impute once and re-impute under each reassignment have finite-population-exact validity under the article's missingness mechanism, with finite-population-valid confidence regions.
Worst-case Wilcoxon--Mann--Whitney testing with arbitrary missing values has statistic bounds and tie-aware p-value safeguards under the ordinary two-sample reference law.
Lower Fisher p-value functions are super-uniform under any fully specified assignment mechanism and can be inverted with guaranteed coverage.
Exact tied Wilcoxon distributions for a fixed completed sample can be computed by generating-polynomial coefficient extraction.
Exact significance tests under restricted sequential randomization rules can be computed by design-specific recursions.
Effect-increasing rank statistics permit exact inversion for bounded null hypotheses and treatment-effect quantiles.
Conditioning on an ex ante covariate-balance partition gives a randomization test with correct unconditional level.
The saved \(\texttt{cvcrand}\) constrained space supports a clustered permutation test based on residualized cluster-mean contrasts.

tldr: Attrition makes both a rank statistic and its randomization reference tail depend on missing sharp-null outcomes. For an explicitly listed rationally weighted fixed-count design, the exact worst-case Wilcoxon-midrank p-value is the maximum over a finite complex of complete weak orders, including equality faces. The envelope is finite-sample valid under arbitrary fixed treatment-indexed observation, computable in \(O((2n+1)^k n|\Omega|\operatorname{poly}(\ell))\) time with a linear one-missing sweep, invertible over additive effects by a finite breakpoint scan, and NP-complete to maximize when \(k\) varies. A saved constrained cluster-randomization support is a concrete conditional-design consumer, provided the endpoint is prespecified and the support is not altered after attrition.

project_justification.gap: Li, Sheng, and Yu obtain a tractable extreme-completion formula under exchangeability and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention, while general Fisher theory assumes that the statistic is evaluable. Neither line characterizes the completion optimizer for an arbitrary explicitly weighted support with ordinary midranks and active equality faces.
project_justification.niche: Complete weak orders are the smallest finite object that simultaneously retains assignment-specific rank sums, active equality faces, and rational certificates.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the chamber representation and validity, identifies the fixed-\(k\) and variable-\(k\) computational boundary, performs exact additive-effect inversion, and gives a support-preserving constrained-cluster corollary.

related_work: Li, Sheng, and Yu study the same nuisance-supremum move in a complete-randomization regime: exchangeability together with their altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention enables an extreme-completion closed form. That simplification does not carry to ordinary midranks and arbitrary explicitly listed rational weights, for which equality faces can be optimal and the complete weak-order chamber optimizer is required. Heng, Zhang, and Feng develop imputation-assisted randomization tests that impute once and re-impute under each reassignment, prove finite-population-exact validity under their missingness mechanism, and construct finite-population-valid confidence regions. Their re-imputation re-randomization law does not evaluate the supplied rational-support Wilcoxon-midrank completion envelope over \(\mathcal C_\delta(a)\). The regime boundary is therefore compact: complete randomization plus altered index tie-breaking gives the Li--Sheng--Yu closed form; arbitrary explicit rational weights plus ordinary midranks gives the equality-inclusive chamber result here; and the complexity of uniform supports generated by fixed-dimensional balance rules remains unresolved. Zeng, Adams, and Bodenham establish arbitrary-missing Wilcoxon bounds and identify tie-induced failures of statistic-only p-value reasoning under the ordinary two-sample law. Luo, Dasgupta, Xie, and Liu establish finite Fisher validity and inversion for fully specified assignment mechanisms with complete evaluability. Sills provides exact tied-rank computation for a fixed completed sample, while Mehta, Patel, and Wei show that restricted randomization can support specialized exact recursions. Karp supplies the polynomial-reduction framework and \(\textsc{Clique}\) source problem used for the explicit-support lower bound. Hennessy et al. justify ex ante conditional randomization partitions, and Yu et al. document the saved constrained space and the distinct residual-contrast \(\texttt{cptest}\) workflow.
technical_internal_limitation: The midrank subset-sum equality characterization and its lowest-tied-block consequence are the load-bearing converse in the \(\textsc{Clique}\) reduction and remain the priority for machine checking. Exact finite enumeration has reproduced the equality-face value \(1\) versus strict-order value \(8/9\), all 210 graph and target instances through four vertices, 1,536 weighted observation schedules, 120 one-missing sweeps, and 145 inversion intervals; these checks are evidence, not proofs.
honest_scope: The stated hardness concerns an explicitly listed rationally weighted support. The three regimes remain separate: Li--Sheng--Yu's complete-randomization result uses exchangeability and altered index tie-breaking; the present result treats arbitrary explicit rational weights and ordinary midranks; and no hardness conclusion is claimed for uniform balance-generated supports or fixed-dimensional balance rules. The fixed-\(k\) bound is \(\mathrm{XP}\), and whether an \(\mathrm{FPT}\) algorithm exists remains open. The constrained-cluster result describes a new prespecified-endpoint rank option; it does not validate unchanged \(\texttt{cptest}\), survivor conditioning, respondent-only endpoints, or conditioning on the selected assignment row. As a direct implementation sanity check, \(k=0\) reduces to the ordinary weighted Fisher test; at a singleton support or when the realized-row mass exceeds \(\alpha\), power can be vacuous.

literature_map.settled: Li, Sheng, and Yu obtain an extreme-completion closed form under exchangeability and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention. Heng, Zhang, and Feng establish finite-population-exact imputation-assisted randomization tests by re-imputing under reassignment and construct finite-population-valid confidence regions.
literature_map.open_boundary: Neither result supplies the exact equality-inclusive optimizer for ordinary midranks under an arbitrary explicitly listed rational assignment law with treatment-indexed masks.

literature_map.thread: Arbitrary missing values in rank tests
literature_map.settled: Statistic bounds, tie-aware warnings, and exact tied Wilcoxon laws for a fixed completed sample are available.
literature_map.open_boundary: None of these papers optimizes the exact assignment-weighted Fisher tail over completion chambers.

literature_map.settled: Finite-population Fisher validity, careful discrete inversion, and effect-increasing rank arguments are established for fully observed outcomes.
literature_map.open_boundary: The inner completion maximum changes at equality faces, so the exact breakpoint set and endpoint inclusion rules remain distinct.

literature_map.settled: Restricted designs can admit specialized exact recursions, tied rank laws admit coefficient extraction, and \(\textsc{Clique}\) is a standard NP-complete source problem.
literature_map.open_boundary: No fixed-\(k\) versus variable-\(k\) classification was found for the explicitly weighted missing-completion optimizer, and hardness for uniform balance-generated supports remains unresolved.

literature_map.settled: Conditioning on an ex ante allocation partition is valid, and \(\texttt{cvcrand}\) carries its saved constrained space into analysis.
literature_map.open_boundary: The documented test is a residual-mean contrast, not an attrition-robust midrank test for a prespecified cluster endpoint.

literature_map.settled: Holding the realized observed subset fixed across reassignment can invalidate inference, while worst-case potential-outcome completion can restore validity.
literature_map.open_boundary: A support-preserving algorithm must allow the observation indicator to depend on treatment and cannot condition on survivors or on the selected support row.

novelty_justification: The nearest result is Li, Sheng, and Yu's supremum Fisher p-value under attrition. Their extreme-completion simplification relies jointly on exchangeability and an altered deterministic unit-index tie-breaking convention. The present kernel retains an arbitrary supplied rational assignment law and ordinary midranks, so the reference tail depends on the completed outcome weak order and equality faces can be optimal. Heng, Zhang, and Feng establish imputation-assisted randomization validity by re-imputing under reassignment and construct valid confidence regions, but their re-randomization law does not evaluate this supplied-support Wilcoxon-midrank completion envelope. The complete equality-inclusive chamber theorem, the \((2n+1)^k\) exact enumeration with a linear one-missing sweep, and the polynomial-bit \(\textsc{Clique}\) converse are therefore distinct field-level contributions. Zeng, Adams, and Bodenham already own arbitrary-missing Wilcoxon bounds and the warning that ties can decouple statistic and p-value extrema; the strict delta is the exact supplied-design tail optimizer and its computational frontier, not the general idea of worst-case rank testing.
